newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sharply higher, led by gas oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sharply higher, led by gas oil.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures finished sharply higher on Thursday as a mixture of fundamental and technical factors pushed prices back to four month highs.
October Brent ended up 48 cents at $20.75 a barrel, below a high for the day at $20.88 and under key technical resistance at $20.80.
IPE gas oil sparked the upward move on Thursday, finishing up $5 a tonne at 1630 GMT, at an increased premium over Brent.
"Gas oil started the move today after breaking some resistance at the open," said an IPE broker.
"These levels look very firm. As far as I can see the only way is up," said another.
The Brent/gas oil crack spread for October widened by 35 cents to finished at $5.30 a barrel.
Dealers said heating oil's strength was a result of low stocks, particularly in the U.S. where inventories are estimated some 15 per cent below year-ago levels.
Traders also said an influential player was seen buying heavily on Thursday, though it was not clear whether to cover short positions or to build a fresh long.
Markets also got a leg up from concerns over the possibility of Caribbean refinery closures due to and possible hurricane damage from storms Eduard and Fran, heading across the Atlantic.
Amerada Hess' huge St Croix, Virgin Islands refinery was seen at risk from Fran.
Dealers also cited news that the U.N. Security Council sanctions committee was considering further investigation of illicit Iraqi gas oil shipments.
They said any investigation might further delay the start of Iraqi exports under the oil-for-food deal.
